title: How it works | ta-amps
description: How the work is organized: tasks and task objects, one real run replayed from its receipts, Herma and Tessera underneath, and the Meta models the workers use.
heading: How it works
lead: Eranos runs on one simple idea that fits almost any project: all work is tasks, and everything a task uses or makes is a task object.

run.heading: A real run, replayed
run.lead: One request, from start to finish, as its own records tell it. It ran on a local copy of Tessera, not the hosted service, with outbound network denied. A builder and an independent reviewer, each holding its own key, did the work on Meta’s contributor-tier model.

facts.data_text: Made-up data only. The public receipt records that no private or nonprofit data and no credential was sent.

run.check: Every hash here recomputes from the run’s files on this site. Each kit file hashes to its SHA-256, the digest covers the four, and each receipt is SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the stored result, as Tessera computes it. Each step’s receipt file says how.

underneath.heading: Underneath
underneath.note: Is a shim the same as RAG? No. RAG pastes search results into a prompt. Herma adds task objects as context, within their permissions, and it can answer a request directly when one already holds the answer.
underneath.run_note: The run above did not pass through Herma: both agents called Tessera and the model directly.
